correctness.rationale: The equilibrium age density is the reset survival divided by the mean wait. Conditional on the age and averaged over the fixed IID reset template, the voter dual gives a connected pair product only when the two walks coalesce. Their separation has jump rate one per direction; the bounded Laplace solution and substitution s=(1−v)²/v give the two beta integrals, convergent exactly for ℓ>p. The short-age tangent bound, Poisson jump tail at each t≤τ₀ and integration by parts give the sign and the advertised cutoff error; taking the gamma-ratio limit and using duplication gives the stated coefficient. Independently at positive temperature, the graphical dual copies at rate γ and is killed by a fresh fair spin at rate κ. Before coalescence both lineages must survive, giving fixed-age covariance E[e^(−2κT)(1−m₀²e^(−2κ(t−T))); T≤t] for the separation walk of rate γ per direction. Its Laplace transform at 2κ is q^ℓ, giving the uniform bound. The law of total covariance then yields the common-age variance; it is positive for biased templates since A is nondegenerate. A separately written ballot/gamma mixture checks four cutoff-sensitive cases numerically. The claim is annealed, not a quenched statement.
residual_risks: The numerical replay is not exact arithmetic or an infinite proof; the frozen numerical support also uses a quadrature approximation and does not test the positive-temperature comparison. The analytic proof supplies the relevant quantifiers.

evidence: The November 2 record combines the identical sharp zero-temperature tail and exact Mellin moment with susceptibility/block fluctuation results and an infinite-mean age limit. The November 8 finding gives the sharper positive-temperature polynomial times exponential tail for symmetric initial spins (and the same exponential upper bound), not a nonzero-mean plateau theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The zero-temperature claim is embedded in a stronger analysis. For the positive-temperature clause distinguish the covered symmetric bound from the elementary biased initial-template age covariance.

evidence: The indexed cutoff proof already bounds the discrepancy by the truncated inverse moment and uses the rate-two Poisson estimate, instead of integrating it in t. Apply that estimate with the cutoff endpoint replaced by each t≤τ₀ and integrate p t^(−p−1) F(t), which directly gives the factor 1+p/(ℓ−p).

At positive temperature the only addition from a nonzero IID mean is a fixed-age boundary value 1−m₀² exp(−2κt) in [0,1] and the variance of the age-dependent mean. Killed-walk comparison and total covariance therefore give the stated plateau and bound without a new asymptotic estimate.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These different presentations do not yield a distinct sharp mechanism or invariant beyond the already covered central result. The cutoff estimate is a routine truncated-moment sharpening and the biased plateau is a conditioning identity.
